I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the steadiest way for me to make a living because I know how to manage it, the buyers are easy to find, and the land and water conditions fit it. At the start of the growing season, I will focus first on my winter wheat that is already in the field, then I will plant summer maize right after wheat harvest. I will not spread my land across too many crops, because with my labor and experience, I would rather do two familiar crops well than chase higher risk. I will use improved or hybrid seed, put on enough fertilizer to protect yield, irrigate at the key times, spray only when needed to keep weeds, insects, and disease under control, and use normal ploughing and rotary tillage so the field stays even and easy for me to manage.
